reforms.description: States responded to the coronavirus pandemic by waiving many licensing requirements, allowing out-of-State licensed professionals to obtain temporary emergency licenses to practice, and permitting retired health workers or students close to graduation to practice temporarily without a license.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing the workforce availability during the pandemic supports economic recovery and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been enacted and are currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms are significant but do not represent a structural change.
reforms.source_quote: States responded to the crisis by waiving many licensing requirements, by allowing out-of-State licensed professionals to obtain temporary emergency licences to practice.

reforms.description: The proposal to make R&D tax credits refundable for new firms aims to enhance innovation by providing financial support to startups engaging in research and development activities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Providing financial support to startups encourages innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposal has been put forward but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: While beneficial, the reform does not represent a major overhaul of the tax system.
reforms.source_quote: Make R&D tax credits refundable for new firms. No action taken.

reforms.description: Inclusionary zoning has been increasingly adopted to ensure affordable housing provision by requiring developers to allocate a portion of new housing units for low-to-moderate income families.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Ensuring affordable housing can support workforce stability and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been enacted and are currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform is significant but does not represent a major systemic change.
reforms.source_quote: Inclusionary zoning has attracted increasing attention since it was introduced in California in the 1970s and appears a way to ensure affordable housing provision.

reforms.description: Several States have enacted reforms to limit the enforceability of non-compete agreements for low-income or low-skilled workers, aiming to enhance worker mobility and wage growth, alongside Massachusetts introducing regulations to make non-compete agreements more employee-friendly, including restrictions on duration and requirements for prior notice and compensation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing worker mobility can lead to better job matches and increased wages, supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been enacted and are currently in effect.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms are important but do not represent a major overhaul of labor laws.
reforms.source_quote: Massachusetts 2018 Regulation to make non-competes more employee-friendly (duration, prior notice, compensation, low-incomes).
